Compute camera-space directions (OpenCV convention: z-forward, y-down, x-right): $d_{cam} = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{i - C_x}{f} \\ -\frac{j - C_y}{f} \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}$ where $C_x = W/2$ and $C_y = H/2$ [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that camera-space directions are computed as $d_{cam} = [ (i - C_x)/f, -(j - C_y)/f, -1 ]^T$ with $C_x = W/2$ and $C_y = H/2$. The provided source code in `src/camera.py` explicitly implements this logic: it sets `cx = W / 2.0` and `cy = H / 2.0` if not provided, and constructs the `dirs` tensor using `(i - cx) / focal`, `-(j - cy) / focal`, and `-torch.ones_like(i)`. The comment in the code also confirms the OpenCV convention and the specific sign flips used.
